subject: Materials Science
title: The LED: Light from a Junction
description: A micro-lesson that makes The LED: Light from a Junction usable.

hook.text: Push current through GaN and it glows blue — electrons falling across the band gap emit photons.

buildup.text: When electrons recombine with holes in a direct band gap material, the energy is released as light.

discovery.text: The band gap determines the color — GaAs (infrared), GaP (green), GaN (blue), InGaN (tunable).

twist.text: White LEDs use a blue LED coated with yellow phosphor — not a white semiconductor, just clever optics.

climax.text: The 2014 Nobel Prize honored blue LED inventors — enabling white LED lighting that saves 15% of global electricity.

punchline.text: A semiconductor junction that turns electrons into photons lit up the world.

quiz.question: How do white LEDs produce white light?
options: They use a white semiconductor material
A blue LED is coated with yellow phosphor to mix wavelengths
They combine red, green, and blue LEDs in one chip
